summary: End-to-end frontend verification of the Closing Inventory auto-save feature in /app/frontend/src/pages/retailer/Dashboard.js. All 4 requested scenarios PASSED: (1) auto-save indicator shows in modal footer (shows 'Auto-saved' with green check after typing); (2) entering a closing qty writes to localStorage under key closing_inventory_{retailerId}_{date}; (3) closing the modal and reopening it restores previously entered values (also shows 'Restored previously entered values' toast); (4) after successful server save (Save Closing -> 'Yes, set all pending as 0'), the localStorage entry is removed.

issues: Sidebar is rendered off-canvas (button reported at left=-248 px) on desktop 1920x1080, the hamburger toggle didn't reliably open it via normal clicks; not part of this feature but worth noting for navigation UX. Test had to invoke .click() via JS on the hidden Closing tab button to reach the feature.

The 'Auto-saving' (blue, spinner) state was effectively skipped in observation because the setTimeout(...,100) flip to 'saved' happens almost immediately; only the green 'Auto-saved' state was actually observable during typing. Functionally fine but the 'saving' visual is essentially never seen by users.

action_items: Optional: Lengthen the 'saving' visible window (e.g., 400-600ms) so users actually see the blue spinner state before it flips to 'Auto-saved'.
Optional: Investigate why the retailer sidebar/drawer doesn't open on desktop 1920x1080 via the hamburger button (pre-existing, unrelated to this feature).
critical_code_review_comments: /app/frontend/src/pages/retailer/Dashboard.js is 7825 lines — far above the 700-line guideline. The closing-inventory logic (state, modal, auto-save helpers at ~2590-2730, modal JSX at ~6860+) should be extracted into a dedicated ClosingInventoryModal component + a useClosingAutoSave hook.

autoSaveClosingToLocalStorage runs on EVERY keystroke (updateClosingQty -> autoSaveClosingToLocalStorage). For 109 products this means writing the full items array to localStorage on each keypress. Consider debouncing (e.g., 300-500ms) to reduce I/O and avoid jank on slow devices.

Storage key uses closingDate, but loadAutoSavedClosing in the openRecordClosingModal flow uses targetDate while the other branch uses today. Confirm the date used at save-time always matches the date used at load-time (so saved data isn't orphaned across day boundaries).

loadAutoSavedClosing comment says 'Only use saved value if it's not empty and server doesn't have a value' but the actual code unconditionally overwrites server value with saved value when savedItem.closing_qty is non-empty. This is acceptable (user's WIP takes precedence) but the comment is misleading — update the comment or add the server-empty guard back if that was the intent.
No quota/size protection — for retailers with thousands of products this could approach localStorage limits. Consider only persisting items whose closing_qty is non-empty.

No expiry / cleanup of stale keys for other dates — if a user enters partial data on day X and never saves, that closing_inventory_{rid}_{X} entry persists forever. Add a cleanup that prunes keys older than N days on modal open.
